- When sentiment shows strong positive spikes (e.g., >0.67) followed by sharp declines, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.33) after a recent uptick, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% to capture mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is stable or mildly positive (0.33–0.67) — add 2–5% bias to forecast for such periods.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements when sentiment is volatile — adjust for 1–3 day lag in price reaction.
- After a sharp sentiment spike (e.g., +1.00), model often overcorrects — apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to prevent overshoot.
- When news volume is constant (as in all examples), sentiment-driven deviations are more pronounced — prioritize sentiment change over price history for correction.
